items.text: It was reported that the costs of medical services and basic goods in Iran have sharply increased. A person said that a surgeon took a 50 million toman bribe for his son's surgery. Also, the prices of ECG, espresso coffee, jacket zipper repair, simple burger, and eyeglass frames have significantly risen.

Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, threatened that if the US attacks again, American military bases in distant regions and even Europe will be targeted. He emphasized that Tehran will not allow even a tiny amount of enriched uranium to leave Iran and has informed Russia of this stance. Meanwhile, Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior advisor to the Commander-in-Chief of the IRGC, said Mojtaba Khamenei has authorized operations anywhere in the world.
A citizen from Bojnord sent a video to Iran International saying that the subsidized flour given to people is full of lice and asked how people are supposed to use this flour.
Niusha Saremi reported that Mojtaba Khamenei has authorized cross-border operations of the IRGC. It was also said that the US and Israel are preparing for confrontation.

Some workers of Homan Gohar Ayandeh Company in the industrial town of Konarak complain about repeated delays in salary payments, working about 14 hours daily, unpaid overtime, and delays in insurance payments, and have called for responsible authorities to intervene. Former workers of Parsilon textile factory in Khorramabad, unemployed and uncertain for about 10 years, have reported the plan for the fourth public auction of the unit and expressed concerns about the capability of the new buyer.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that while the US government talks about continuing economic pressure and naval blockade instead of war and some media report progress in negotiations, field evidence indicates readiness for the possibility of military conflict.

A video released on social media shows the restlessness and grief of the mother of the missing Peyman Pourdavarani in the absence of her son. Peyman, 31 years old and father of one child, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Kerman.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi announced on the evening of Wednesday, 20 Aban that Ali Zaghi and Ilya Akbari, two young men arrested during the national uprising of Dey month, face imminent execution. The Mashhad Revolutionary Court, headed by Hossein Yazdankhah, has sentenced these two young men to death. Additionally, four other young men in the Shandiz case have also been sentenced to death.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced on Wednesday, 20 Aban, that Washington seeks a "complete victory" in the war and does not intend to accept any result less than that. He said rebuilding what the US has destroyed will take 25 years and hopes not to have to destroy more parts of the country. Trump also said Iran has been at war against the US since 1979 and that the US did not start the war.

On Wednesday, 20 Aban, a group of Havaniruz employees protested the uncertainty of the housing cooperative project by staging a sit-in in front of Kermanshah Governor's Office. Also, employees of the Isfahan Regional Electricity Company held a protest in front of their company building. Yesterday, Shahin voucher holders gathered at the Saipa administrative building to protest the non-delivery of their registered vehicles despite payment and missed deadlines.
It was reported that the Iranian government has issued a military ultimatum to NATO and European countries.

The Law on Regulation and Supervision of Border Trade and Sustainable Employment for Border Residents, approved on 25 Bahman 1402, obliges the government to plan for sustainable employment, sufficient income, and proper social security. The main question is how these obligations will translate into clear and actionable support in daily life. This issue is especially relevant for porters whose income depends on border trade.

A video released on social media shows the restlessness of the mother of the disappeared Ghazal Janqorban at her grave. Ghazal, 15 years old, was shot by suppressors during the public protests on 19 Dey in Isfahan and died in the hospital.

More than 135 days have passed since the arrest of Fatemeh Jami, a citizen of Gorgan, and she is still being held in Gorgan prison without a clear status. A source close to her family has confirmed this. The court hearing for her case is scheduled for 1 Azar.

Kiumars Heydari, deputy chief of staff of the Islamic Republic Armed Forces, said the confrontation with the US has turned into a regional war and the enemy's interests and military bases are within range of the Islamic Republic's missiles and drones. He added that the armed forces' response will be without geographic limitation and if an aircraft takes off from a country to attack Iran, the armed forces are allowed to target a similar target in that country. He also said the armed forces' target bank for a possible future war has been updated and covers points in the region and beyond.
In the audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad, a warning of an attack on Europe by the Islamic Republic was raised.

Alireza Koushki, Esteghlal player, said he went three times close to death due to a severe injury. He explained that an elbow hit from a young player caused a rib fracture and pressure on his lung. Doctors stated about 50% of his lung was filled with air, and he has undergone a difficult treatment period.

Adidas celebrated the farewell to the German national team by printing images of German football legends on the last jersey designed for the team. The German Football Federation's contract with Adidas ends at the end of 2026 after 72 years, and Nike will design and produce the German national teams' kits thereafter. The upcoming FIFA international match dates will feature Germany's last games wearing Adidas kits.

Israeli company Rafael unveiled the "Super Ice" cruise missile with a 454-kilogram warhead. Farzin Nadimi said this missile, with a speed close to the speed of sound and advanced guidance systems, can target from farther distances with greater accuracy. Nadimi added that the more powerful warhead and increased resistance to navigation disruptions have enhanced the missile's operational capability, and it is still unclear to what extent these technologies will be used in a potential conflict with the Islamic Republic.

A new wave of bomb threats against schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, and Italy has led to the emergency evacuation of several educational centers. Italian officials stated that about 6,300 schools have been affected by these threats. Reza Talebi said Russia might be using cyber groups and networks linked to the Islamic Republic to create crisis and increase divisions in European societies.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, said they will not allow even a tiny amount of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran. He added that these materials will remain for domestic use in Iran and that the Islamic Republic is designing nuclear-powered ships and submarines. Rezaei also said that in the future, these materials might be used to build small modular reactors.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that a power struggle over Ali Khamenei's legacy has escalated. He added that after Khamenei's death, power factions within the IRGC have clashed to seize a larger share of power and wealth and to eliminate their rivals. He also said that the battle between Mohsen Rezaei and Baqer Qalibaf has become one of the most visible manifestations of the power struggle at the top of the Islamic Republic.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that after Khamenei's death, the power struggle in the Islamic Republic intensified. He added that Qalibaf, who had long aspired to the presidency, tried to present himself as beyond the president and as the main decision-maker of the system. Qalibaf claimed to have coordinated the heads of the branches of power, IRGC commanders, and managed the war.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said if no agreement is reached between the US and the Islamic Republic, a military attack by the US and Israel will inevitably happen sooner or later; because Washington and Tel Aviv consider the Islamic Republic's potential acquisition of nuclear bombs and intercontinental missiles a threat to their national security.

Despite expectations for a reduction in tensions in the war between the Islamic Republic and the United States, attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz continue. According to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, at least 10 ships were targeted in the first 10 days of November. The Islamic Republic has claimed responsibility for attacking three oil tankers on Sunday, 17 Aban [Gregorian: 2026-11-08].

The New York Times on Wednesday, 20 Aban, reported citing three Iraqi officials and one American official that Washington's weeks-long effort to persuade Iraq, Turkey, and Pakistan to close border crossings with Iran has so far been unsuccessful. The US has requested the closure of all Iranian border crossings except two, but Baghdad has rejected this request. After diplomatic efforts failed, the US Central Command formed a 20-member task force called "Iron Gate" to counter the transfer of weapons and sanctioned goods through Iran's borders.

Iran International's investigation shows that Parsian Bank has been managed for years by the Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order. The Order appoints the bank's managers and has gradually transferred the bank's shares to its subsidiary holding, Tadbir. Key figures from the Order are present at the bank's top levels.

Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Instagram the start of production of his first TV series called "Day 1s." The series is about a British agent in the football transfer world and is being made in collaboration with Matthew Vaughn. Ronaldo will be the executive producer of the series and may also appear on camera.

Shahram Khaledi said Russia's new proposal on the Islamic Republic's nuclear program should be viewed within the framework of Moscow's competition with Washington. He added that Moscow does not want Iran to gain the capability to build nuclear weapons and may be seeking a way out of the crisis. Khaledi also mentioned the possibility of Iraq mediating between Tehran and Washington, saying Baghdad may be trying to create conditions for an agreement.

Baharan Azadi, author of two articles about the widespread gas outage, was a guest on the program "With Kambiz Hosseini" to discuss people's accounts of the outage and its impact on their daily lives in Iran.

Kambiz Hosseini warned of an unprecedented gas outage and a harsh winter in Iran. Some children go to school with blankets, and the government’s plan to keep people warm is saving energy. The term "energy imbalance" reflects the reality of people's lives with cold homes and worried elderly and students.

Saudi Civil Defense announced that remnants of two ballistic missiles fired by Yemeni Houthis towards the Mecca region fell on Wednesday in areas including the village of Sabouha after being intercepted and destroyed. On the same day, the Saudi-led military coalition reported intercepting and destroying a drone in the eastern region of the country. The eastern region of Saudi Arabia, which hosts major oil and gas reserves and key Aramco facilities, had also been targeted by drone attacks in recent days.

A video published on social media shows the poor condition of Taq Kasra, a structure over 1400 years old near Baghdad. The video shows the area around this historical heritage site filled with garbage, depicting neglect of one of the architectural masterpieces of the Sasanian era in the heart of Ctesiphon, the capital of the Sasanian Empire.

G7 foreign ministers condemned the destabilizing policies of the Islamic Republic in the final statement of the Paris meeting and called for full implementation of the reinstated UN sanctions. They deemed maritime attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the security conspiracies of the Revolutionary Guard in Western countries unacceptable. G7 member countries warned that if a diplomatic solution is not reached, economic and political pressures on the Islamic Republic will intensify.

Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, spokesperson for the Pakistan Army, stated that his country is ready to take all necessary measures to defend Saudi Arabia based on the joint defense agreement and the Makkah Pact. He emphasized that Pakistan's commitment to Saudi Arabia's security is non-negotiable and confirmed that Pakistani forces are currently present in Saudi Arabia with defensive, support, and exercise missions. The meeting on 26 October of representatives of the Makkah Pact member countries with officials of the Islamic Republic in Tehran was held to reduce tensions and strengthen regional cooperation.

The Wall Street Journal reported, citing American and regional officials, that JD Vance, the Vice President of the United States, is considering direct negotiations with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic. Vance is leading Washington's diplomatic efforts to reach an agreement with Tehran, and Donald Trump has approved his role in these negotiations.

Simultaneously with concerns about the execution sentence of Peyman Farahavar, a prisoner poet in Lakan prison in Rasht, the office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the risk of executing death sentences for six detainees of the December national uprising. According to the statement, Ali Zaghi, Ilya Akbari, and four other young men have been sentenced to death in the so-called Shandiz case. The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi called for widespread information dissemination to prevent the execution of these sentences.

Mohammad Qaedi, an international relations lecturer, said that Donald Trump seeks to use the full military and economic capacity of the US to gain more concessions from the Islamic Republic. He added that Trump does not desire a large-scale war and tries to reach an agreement by oscillating between negotiation and economic pressure, which he can present as an achievement to the American public.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board of directors has considered removing Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, after the disclosure of his second extramarital affair. One of these relationships was with a woman suspected of collaborating with China's intelligence agency. Nvidia's board was scheduled to decide on Huang's future on Wednesday.

Hossein Taeb said Mohsen Rezaei's trip to Moscow was in response to a written message from Vladimir Putin to Mojtaba Khamenei. He added that Trump sent a representative to Putin before the US elections to pave the way for negotiations with the Islamic Republic. Taeb said the US must first accept seven conditions of the Islamic Republic, then Tehran will decide on negotiations.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, a journalist and political analyst, referred to a Wall Street Journal report about the possibility of JD Vance meeting Mohsen Rezaee and said the Trump administration is pursuing three paths simultaneously against the Islamic Republic: agreement, economic pressure, and military action. He also emphasized that denying changes in the composition of the Islamic Republic's negotiation team means continuing the "neither war nor peace" strategy. The regional threats by government officials indicate that Tehran is preparing for the possibility of war.

The spokesperson of the Pakistan Army announced that Islamabad is ready to quickly deploy forces to Saudi Arabia based on the Mecca defense pact, and Pakistani forces are currently stationed in the country for support and defensive operations.

Zinedine Zidane, the coach of the French national team, said he would like to coach Juventus someday and that the future is never certain. He also spoke about the impact of Italian football on his career and the absence of many players from his team, including Kylian Mbappé, who will miss the next match due to pain but is expected to be available on Sunday.
Behrouz Saeedi, a citizen from Takab, was sentenced to five years, six months, and one day in prison by the Revolutionary Court of that city.

Yisrael Katz, Israel's Defense Minister, said the country has acted decisively and prudently against the Islamic Republic in full coordination with the army and will continue this approach according to the conditions. He added that issuing orders for targeted operations in Gaza, defensive and offensive operations in Lebanon, and maintaining the security zone in Syria does not require approval from political opponents or any legal authority. The Defense Minister said government security decisions are made within existing and appropriate oversight frameworks.
Videos published on social media show that women and men gathered at night at Si-o-se-pol in Isfahan and danced and sang.

Stephen Curry, the star player of the Golden State Warriors basketball team, was injured in the abdomen and right flank during the first quarter of the game against the Houston Rockets and left the stadium for an MRI. Steve Kerr, the Warriors coach, said Curry has never experienced such pain before and the extent of his absence is unknown. Curry's exit ended the Warriors' eight-game winning streak and the team lost 115-108 to the Rockets.

The Israeli army and Shin Bet announced that in last night's airstrike on the Nasser Hospital complex in Khan Yunis, a senior Hamas commander and several members of the group were targeted. Israeli officials said Hamas used the hospital premises for military activities and weapons storage. Hamas officials stated that six people were killed in this attack.

Benjamin Haddad, France's European Affairs Minister, said Paris will cooperate with its European partners to intensify sanctions against the Islamic Republic, especially those responsible for the cyberattack on store cooling systems. This action is in response to an attack that France holds the Islamic Republic responsible for. The French Foreign Ministry identified the cyber unit 'Shaheed Kaveh' affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards as responsible for the attack on over 700 stores.

Mosib Khoshsaleqe, a 22-year-old citizen from Khaf, has been held in custody in Torbat Heydariyeh prison for over 109 days without a final decision. His court session was held on 11 Aban at the Torbat Heydariyeh Revolutionary Court, but no verdict has been issued yet. He is accused of insulting sacred things and blasphemy against the Prophet.

A video was sent to Iran International in which a citizen at the eternal grave of Danial Diani emphasized continuing resistance in difficult conditions, saying that this resistance will continue in memory of the killed until the current Islamic Republic leaves.

Persepolis club published a sale advertisement for Amirhossein Mahmoudi, a 19-year-old player, in a newspaper. This action was taken after Mahmoudi openly criticized the club management and was excluded from training sessions. The club's reaction by publishing the sale ad is seen as punitive and controversial.

An eighth-grade student in the city of Sadra, Fars province, was physically punished by the school assistant. Following the release of a video of the incident, the director of education in Sadra announced that a written warning was issued to the school assistant.

Masoud Pezeshkian focused on the environmental damages of war in Iran and Gaza at the UN climate summit; meanwhile, Iran's internal environmental crises, from drying wetlands and Lake Urmia to air pollution, forest fires, and water and electricity shortages, were not reflected in his speech.

Iran International viewers have reported a reduction in bakers' flour quotas, poor flour quality, and the closure of some bakeries. Some citizens have also reported the presence of insects and animal waste in the flour they use.

The Pas-de-Calais prefecture in northern France announced it is investigating a possible bomb threat at the Calais-Frethun train station; this announcement came one day after bomb threats to schools in Italy, the UK, and Ireland and following a wave of bomb threats in Europe. The prefecture urged people to follow the latest updates from official accounts of the French railway company.

A video received by Iran International shows the condition of Rasht's market in Aban 1405. Some viewers describe the city's market as "quiet and less crowded than last year." During the protests in Dey 1404 in Rasht, security forces caused the deaths of several citizens by trapping protesters in a market fire and preventing aid.

Reza Saalabi, a political prisoner from Ahvaz, is serving his 12-year sentence in Yazd Central Prison. After four years in Sheiban Prison in Ahvaz, he was exiled to Yazd Prison and has been there for over four years without furlough or in-person visits with his family. This information was reported by HRANA news agency.

Mohammad Mokhber, advisor to Mojtaba Khamenei, said the Supreme Leader's message about having no geographical limitation in responding to the enemy indirectly means removing missile range restrictions. Mokhber said on 21 Aban that there is no doubt about the recurrence of war, and the longer the war lasts, the higher the chance of victory for the Islamic Republic. He called the Islamic Republic's victory certain and said the Americans will sink deeper into the "quagmire they created" the longer they continue the war.

A video received shows that workers of Hormozgan Steel Company protested on Aban 21 by gathering in the yard of Abad Rahaan Pars Company in Bandar Abbas, protesting the non-payment of their four months' salaries.

Georgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, stated that so far no real danger has been seen in the school bomb threats. More than six thousand schools were evacuated yesterday, and investigations to identify the perpetrators of the threats continue.

The director of education in District One of Karaj reported the investigation of a teacher who emptied the contents of a trash bin on a student's head. The teacher was summoned to the education supervisory department, received a serious warning, and was banned from continuing to attend the school.

The final day of the COP 31 leaders' summit in Antalya is being held with a focus on turning climate commitments into executable projects. On the first day, Norway, Britain, and Canada announced a joint initiative to provide 10 billion dollars in climate finance by 2030.

Argentina's Foreign Ministry called the Islamic Republic's designation of its navy and air force as terrorist baseless and unacceptable. The ministry accused Tehran of refusing judicial cooperation and handing over wanted individuals. It was mentioned that the Islamic Republic was involved in the terrorist attacks in Buenos Aires in 1992 and 1994.

A citizen reacted in a video sent to Iran International to the advertising phrase "zero inflation" on heavy vehicles and said this slogan belonged to the Hoeyda era and people today feel price increases in daily life.
Amin Ghodousian, a citizen from Rask who was arrested by Intelligence Department forces in Chabahar one month ago, has been transferred to Zahedan prison.

The Iraqi parliament and government have started investigations into the smuggling of the country's oil through Iran to Afghanistan. Heybat al-Halbousi, the Speaker of the Iraqi Parliament, announced the formation of a temporary committee to examine the theft of oil from Kirkuk and the Kurdistan Region. The Iraqi Prime Minister also ordered an investigation into oil smuggling in areas controlled by the Kata'ib Hezbollah militias.
Mohammad Baharmast Ziyabari, a resident of Ziyabar city, was released on bail of three billion tomans from the West Gilan penitentiary. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Benyamin Soltanian won a gold medal in taekwondo and the Iranian women's national futsal team won bronze, marking Iran's first team medal in Olympic history. Iran stands 32nd in the games with 8 medals.

A video released on social media shows the mourning of the mother and sister of the martyr Mohammad Shakerami Chegni at his grave. Mohammad was shot twice during the protests on 19 Dey 1404 in Khorramabad and died hours later.

Reuters reported on Thursday, 21 Aban that two Iranian men in the UK were convicted by a court for cooperating with the Islamic Republic's intelligence agency and spying on Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, journalists of Iran International. The UK police stated that this case indicates an increase in the Islamic Republic's intelligence activities in the country.

The head of Tehran's major crimes police reported the arrest of a man in west Tehran on charges of sexual assault against a young woman. According to this police official, the suspect also extorted the complainant by threatening to release private images.

Yadollah Gholami, a player of Iran's amputee national football team, announced in a video on his Instagram page that Iran will not participate in the World Cup in Mexico. He said that due to the incompetence of officials, Iran could not attend the World Cup. Gholami added that last year Iran became Asian champion in Jakarta, Indonesia, and earned the right to participate in the World Cup, but one day before departure they were told there was no budget and the country's airspace was closed.

Ehsan Sohrabi, a labor activist, announced that according to published reports, the price of domestically produced medicines has increased by about 150 percent since the beginning of the year, and the price of some foreign medicines has risen by up to 400 and in some cases 500 percent. He warned that the sharp increase in the cost of medicine and medical services could deprive some patients of treatment. Sohrabi also considered the increased visits to public medical centers as a sign of citizens' reduced financial ability to use private sector services.

A group of dismissed workers and job-seeking youth from the city of Hur and the Haft-Tappeh area protested against long-term unemployment and their critical livelihood situation. These individuals held a protest gathering and sit-in in front of the Haft-Tappeh Sugarcane Company gate, demanding the resolution of unemployment issues and attention to their demands.

A video released on social media shows the family of Naser Nasiri at his grave. Naser Nasiri, a 52-year-old father, was killed by a direct shot from a military bullet during the January 9 protests in Tehran in Azadshahr town.

The Judiciary Media Center announced the appointment of Gholamreza Sarlak as the new director general of prisons in Semnan province. Gholamreza Sarlak previously served as the director general of prisons in Golestan province and is accused of widespread human rights violations during his tenure there. These include carrying out death sentences, failure to separate prisoners by crime, and deaths of prisoners due to lack of timely medical services.

Italian government sources reported that about 1,800 schools in the country received emails containing bomb threats on Thursday, 21 Aban. This is the second consecutive day of widespread sending of such messages to schools in Italy. Ansa news agency reported that some schools were evacuated after receiving these emails.

Malikeh (Fatemeh) Haghighat, a resident of Gorgan, has been held in detention in the city's prison for over 3 months without a clear judicial status. She faces charges including propaganda against the regime, and her court hearing is scheduled for November 17. Temporary release on bail has not been granted so far.

The Assembly of Experts issued a statement saying that reviewing Iran's exit from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and revising the country's defense doctrine has become an unavoidable necessity and a national demand. The Assembly referred to repeated threats from enemies, especially against Iran's nuclear knowledge, and stated that no hope can be placed in international bodies responsible in this area. It also warned that if another attack by enemies begins, Iran's armed forces will respond immediately and without geographical limitation.

Information received by Iran International indicates that security agencies have intensified pressure on the families seeking justice on the eve of the first anniversary of the killing of the Dey month protesters. Security agents have summoned and threatened families, warning that if they use the title "Javidnam," their names will be placed on the terrorist list. These agencies have also prevented the holding of anniversary ceremonies and promised government benefits to families in exchange for accepting the title "martyr."

Donald Trump said in a Truth Social message that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and holds hundreds of billions of dollars of Iran's money and controls their strait. He also wrote that he asked JD Vance to focus entirely on corruption and widespread crimes. Reuters reported that Vance has recently been involved in efforts to establish contact with Iran.

A number of political and civil activists issued a joint statement protesting the increase in executions in Iran, especially in political and security cases, and called for an immediate and unconditional halt to executions. They referred to the executions of detainees from the December 1404 protests and violations of fair trial principles. The signatories emphasized that executions neither deter nor help solve problems and called for an immediate stop to executions as a necessary step for realizing civil rights and sustainable security.

The publication of a sale advertisement for Amirhossein Mahmoudi, a young Persepolis player, in a newspaper has been met with protest from Mehdi Tartar, the team's coach. Tartar criticized the advertisement's release without coordination with the coaching staff and intended to return Mahmoudi to group training after a discussion. A Persepolis official said the ad was published for financial transparency and due to the club's stock market status, and it does not mean Mahmoudi's sale is definite.

A court in Britain found Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi-Mansh guilty of aiding the Islamic Republic's intelligence service in spying on two Iran International journalists. Sepahvand was found guilty unanimously on two charges of aiding a foreign intelligence service and intent to carry out a violent attack. Their sentencing is scheduled for December 17 at 14:00 at the Old Bailey court in London.

The Iranian Teachers' Trade Union condemned the widespread issuance of death sentences following the protests of Dey 1404. The statement referred to the killing of a significant number of citizens, especially young people, and described the increase in issuing and carrying out death sentences for detained protesters as a sign of using this punishment as a tool to create fear and suppress society. The union also emphasized the right of young people to have a future full of hope, freedom, and dignified life.

The board of directors of the American company Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as CEO and other managerial roles. Colette Kress, the executive vice president and chief financial officer, has accepted to act as interim head of Nvidia until a new CEO is selected. Huang's resignation was announced after pressure due to the disclosure of two extramarital relationships, including one with a Chinese woman suspected of collaborating with Beijing's intelligence agencies.

Iranian users on social media, amid war and increasing economic pressures, write about fatigue, livelihood uncertainty, and concerns about the possible start of a new round of attacks. Statements by Islamic Republic officials about people's resilience have also faced widespread reactions from users. Adaleh Borang, a member of the Iran International editorial team, talks about these reactions.

Elina Hojati's mother said in a video that her daughter was killed by a "war bullet." She referred to Elina's academic achievements and emphasized she will never forgive the perpetrators of the murder. Elina, a 23-year-old student, was killed by Islamic Republic agents in Tehran on the evening of 18 Dey.

Information received by Iran International indicates that managers and officials of some high schools in Shiraz subject students to extensive body searches. Students say the school staff touch all parts of their bodies during inspections, causing discomfort and embarrassment. Last month, a student from Fazli Technical School in Fardis told Iran International that the school staff touch students' private parts during searches and face harsher treatment if they protest.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic will fail due to Tehran's opposition to withdrawing from its nuclear program. He added that if the siege continues, the Islamic Republic may take actions that could pave the way for another US military attack.

The family of Asieh Ramazani stated in a video and text that their grief and longing continue 10 months after her killing. Asieh, a mother of two, was killed by direct gunfire from Islamic Republic forces during the protests on 19 Dey 1404 in Tehran at the age of 39.

The Israeli Prime Minister's office denied reports of a severe verbal dispute between Netanyahu and Trump during a phone call about resuming military attacks on Iran. Netanyahu's office called the news fake and baseless. Sources said the call was tense, but a senior Israeli official said the conversation was not difficult.

Vicky Evans, Deputy Police Commissioner and Senior National Coordinator of the UK Counter-Terrorism Police, said in an exclusive interview with Iran International that evidence presented in court shows the order to carry out this operation was issued by individuals linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

According to Reuters, Nvidia's board is considering removing Jensen Huang, the company's CEO, following reports about his personal relationships and the start of an internal US investigation, and he has resigned from this position. Nvidia's shares fell about seven percent in early Frankfurt trading. These developments coincide with the investigation of a woman named Alice Huang's role in the possible transfer of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and increased pressure from US lawmakers for stricter chip export restrictions to China.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center announced that the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz is "severe" and there is a high likelihood of further attacks on oil tankers and other vessels in the area. Four attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf have been recorded in the past 96 hours. The center warned that the likelihood of more attacks, especially near the coast of Musandam, Oman, is very high.

Police reported a shooting of five people in the Logan Circle area of Washington, about one and a half kilometers from the White House. Police forces are providing the latest information about this incident.

Javad Khaki, a political prisoner, returned to the Central Prison of Karaj after the end of his leave. According to the Harana news agency, he returned to prison today, Thursday, 21 Aban. Khaki had been granted leave on 10 Aban.

Mark Rutte, NATO Secretary General, evaluated the Abu Dhabi talks positively and described the positions of the US, Europe, and Ukraine in these talks as very coordinated. However, Volodymyr Zelensky, President of Ukraine, described the US approach to talks with Russia about the new security order as "strange."

Washington police announced that in a shooting on Thursday morning inside a gym in the Logan Circle neighborhood, one person was killed and four were injured, one of whom is in critical condition. The suspect barricaded himself in an apartment on the seventh floor of a residential building and was found by police after about an hour with a self-inflicted gunshot wound and has died. The motive for the shooting is still unknown.

A video released on social media shows moments of the immortal dance of Behnam Kashani, a 33-year-old tattoo artist. He was killed on 18 Dey during protests in front of the intelligence building in Mahallat city, Markazi province, by gunfire from suppression forces.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation suspended Yaser Asani, Esteghlal winger, for two matches due to misconduct towards the referee in the match against Esteghlal Khuzestan, with one match suspended, and fined him 500 million tomans. Alireza Ildarom, the assistant referee, was suspended from refereeing for two months due to misconduct towards Asani. Esteghlal and Tractor clubs were each fined 500 million tomans due to fan behavior and spectator chants, and the return match between Tractor and Malavan will be played without spectators.

Mehr news agency on Thursday, 21 Aban 1405 reported a video from the sky of Tehran and announced that the Islamic Republic's armed forces tested "new missiles" in the west of Iran's capital. Received images from citizens show the launch of three missiles from the Bidganeh area.

Anita Anand, Canada's Foreign Minister, announced that Ottawa voted against the Islamic Republic's membership in the "Programme and Coordination Committee" in a secret vote at the UN General Assembly. Anand said the Islamic Republic suppresses opponents and fuels instability in the Middle East. She added that a government with such a record is not qualified to be a member of a body tasked with upholding the UN Charter.

According to rescuers, three wooden boats that arrived on Thursday, 21 Aban, at the port of La Restinga on El Hierro island, one of the Canary Islands of Spain, carried more than 150 migrants who had been at sea for nearly a week. Fernando Clavijo, head of the local government of the Canary Islands, announced that from 10 to 19 Aban, 7,432 migrants had entered these islands and warned about the increase in migration via the Atlantic route. Clavijo said authorities had previously received warnings and information about increased boat movements from West Africa.
